g.text: 0 · Today: the ring
A lane all round, one car deep in the middle.
Every corner turns at 0.2 (red): no car can drive it.
7 cars on 2 tiles
A · Straight street, two tiles
In at one end, out at the other, one way.
The two turns at 0.45 eat the ends of the front row.
12 cars on 2 tiles
B · Straight street, three tiles
The same, a tile longer: each tile more adds
about eight, against the ring's five.
21 cars on 3 tiles
C · On the corner
In off the side street straight down the aisle,
out onto the high street: one turn, not two.
14 cars on 2 tiles
D · Round the corner
An L: in off the side street, round, out onto
the high street. Three turns leave little room.
16 cars on 3 tiles
E · One tile
In and out of one tile is a U-turn at 0.35 (red),
and nothing fits beside it.
0 cars on 1 tile
F · The street stops short
One tile on the street: a loop back out the
same tile, turning at 0.3 (red).
5 cars on 2 tiles
Key
the way cars drive, one way
a turn tighter than a car turns (0.45)
A tile is 60 px (12 m). A car 0.29 × 0.15, an aisle 0.22,
bays at 60° and 0.2 across. Bays are placed by test:
wholly on the lot, clear of every aisle and of each other.
